newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Doctors' strike hits Sri Lanka hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Doctors' strike hits Sri Lanka hospitals.

text.p: A half-day doctors' strike hit about 700 Sri Lankan hospitals on Thursday, reducing services to emergencies only, the Government Medical Officers' Association said.
The association, which represents nearly 4,000 of the island's 4,500 Western-qualified doctors, said they would strike again if their demand for higher wages is not met.
"We will call a one-day token strike for March 5 if no solution is in sight," said association assistant secretary A.L. Fernando.
Hospitals throughout the country only attended to emergencies on Thursday morning. Other patients were turned away, doctors said.
The association is pushing for higher doctors' salaries to match those of judges.
Health Minister A.H.M. Fowzie branded the strike "anti-social" and said the demand was unfair as doctors could practise outside their government jobs, but judges could not.
